To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glycome of IVIg and SCIg preparations is highly heterogeneous, and that the glycan composition of IVIg is different from the glycan composition in SCIg.
the glycosylation profile of the IgG antibodies present in the IVIg/SCIG preparations is a major determinant of their anti-inflammatory effects.
IVIg preparations have a wide range in terms of protein‐glycan interactions, which are likely to be important for the immunoregulating effects of IVIgs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel targets for IVIg/ SCIg and with the development of novel therapeutic approaches based on the use of IVIg.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of action of immunoglobulin (IG) preparations and their application in the treatment of immune‐related diseases.
elucidation of the mechanisms of the immunomodulatory effects of IVIG/SCIg.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IVIg/SCIG is an immunomodulatory drug that is effective in a wide variety of autoimmune and inflammatory diseases and that it has a very low incidence of serious adverse events.
IVIg/SCIG are not only immunoglobulin replacement therapy, but also immunomodulatory agents, which have a wide spectrum of effects on different cells and molecules.
the mechanisms of action are not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the role of protein-glycan interactions as targets in the mechanism of action of intravenous/sub-cutaneous immunoglobulin preparations (IVIg /SCIg) and that we have developed a novel approach for the identification of the target glycan structures.
the IVIg/ SCIg preparations have the ability to interact with glycan moieties of the target proteins, and this ability is a key factor that contributes to the clinical efficacy of IVIg.
IVIg/SCIG preparations are not just a mixture of antibodies with different specificities, but rather a complex cocktail of different glycoforms of antibodies, each with its own biological activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein‐glycan interactions are an important target for IVIg/ SCIg preparations, and that this target is not only relevant to IgG‐Fc‐dependent functions, but also to other IgG‐dependent functions.
the glycan structures of the IgG molecules contained in IVIg/ SCIg preparations may have an important role in their therapeutic effects.
the carbohydrate moiety of IgG is important for the anti-inflammatory effects of IVIq/SCIg.
